## What is publicly documented

::: {.case-evidence}
ESIIL STARS includes Oglala Lakota College. Observing Unci Maka describes community-developed earth-observation methods.
:::

Sources: [ESIIL: ESIIL STARS](https://esiil.org/esiil-stars); [ESIIL: Observing Unci Maka](https://esiil.org/working-groups/observing-unci-maka). Reviewed October 14, 2026.

## Relationship status

Existing ESIIL educational relationships are documented; participation in this proposed series is not confirmed.

## A proposed question to discuss

Which relationships among grassland fire, grazing, drought and community priorities would participating Nations want to examine?

This question was drafted for the prototype; it is not attributed to the Nation, organization or practitioners.

## A possible learning contribution

Begin with the existing relationships and each Nation’s own definitions of useful evidence.

## What remains context-specific

Study areas, culturally important outcomes and release decisions remain specific to each participating Nation.

## Link to regional context

The [fire-history module](../history.qmd) includes a broad regional window associated with this discussion. Its event counts describe that rectangle, not this Nation or organization. Regional adjacency does not establish a research relationship or shared authority.
